sentiment.rationale: Management raised comparable currency-neutral EPS growth guidance to approximately 8% for 2025, up from a prior expectation, and affirmed organic revenue growth of 5%-6%. The raise is organic, driven by faster productivity realization and disciplined cost management, not FX or one-time items. However, the raise is modest and management explicitly acknowledges a 5% currency headwind to EPS and a 1%-2% headwind to revenue, tempering the overall positive signal.

summary.revenue: Organic revenue grew 5% in Q2 2025. Price/mix increased 6%, driven by approximately five points of pricing actions and one point of favorable mix.
summary.eps: Comparable EPS reached $0.87, up 4% year-over-year, despite 5% currency headwinds and a higher effective tax rate.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 organic revenue growth expected at 5%-6%. Comparable currency-neutral EPS growth expected at approximately 8%. Comparable EPS growth of approximately 3% versus $2.88 in 2024, including a 5% currency headwind.
summary.margin: Comparable gross margin increased approximately 80 basis points; comparable operating margin increased approximately 190 basis points. Approximately one-third of underlying expansion driven by faster realization of productivity initiatives.
key_risks: Currency headwinds: 1%-2% headwind to comparable net revenues and 5% headwind to comparable EPS for full year 2025.
Volume decline: Global unit case volume declined 1% in Q2, impacted by adverse weather, difficult prior year comparisons, and consumer pressure in select markets.
Capacity constraints: Fairlife volume growth moderating due to capacity constraints until New York facility comes online in early 2026.
Geopolitical and weather disruptions: Early monsoons in India, geopolitical conflict, and hurricane in Mexico impacted Q2 volume.
Consumer pressure: Pressure on lower-income socioeconomic segments in North America and other markets.
key_opportunities: Productivity initiatives: Faster realization of productivity initiatives, especially from marketing transformation and disciplined operating expense management, contributed to margin expansion.
Innovation: Sprite became number three sparkling soft drink in the US following new variants; Sprite Plus Tea scaled based on strong consumer demand.
Value share gains: Seventeenth consecutive quarter of value share gains globally.
Fairlife growth: Double-digit volume growth in Q2, with capacity expansion expected in early 2026.
Marketing transformation: Digital tools, AI-based pack price optimization, and locally relevant campaigns driving growth.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management stated, 'We're confident we can navigate varying local market dynamics during the remainder of 2025 to deliver on our updated guidance,' and 'we have great confidence we will deliver on our updated 2025 guidance and create enduring value for our stakeholders.'
